title: The box under the bed
body: My grandma keeps a small wooden box under her bed. Inside there is a collection of buttons — glass ones, wooden ones, one made of silk thread. Last winter I asked her to throw the box away. Our new flat was small. "These are not valuable," I said. She opened the box so that I could look more closely. Each button came from a coat, and each coat came from a year. The white one was from her wedding coat. The small brown one was from my father's first school jacket. "A thing is not valuable because of its price," she said. Now the box sits on our new shelf. My little cousin likes to count the buttons. She is so careful that grandma lets her hold the white one. Some collections are not about the things at all.

questions.q: Why did the writer want to throw the box away?
options: Because the buttons were broken.
Because the new flat was small and he thought the buttons were not valuable.
Because grandma asked him to do it.
Because his cousin wanted a new box.
questions.explanation: 'Last winter I asked her to throw the box away. Our new flat was small. "These are not valuable," I said.'

questions.q: Why did grandma open the box?
options: To find a white button.
To show her wedding coat.
To count the buttons with her grandson.
So that he could look at the buttons more closely.
questions.explanation: 'She opened the box so that I could look more closely.'

questions.q: What does the last sentence mean?
options: A collection can be about memories, not things.
Collections should be kept under a bed.
Old buttons are worth a lot of money.
Children should not touch old things.
questions.explanation: 'Some collections are not about the things at all.' 与 '"A thing is not valuable because of its price"' 呼应,指收藏承载的是记忆。

title: The pattern on the scarf
body: Our art teacher brought an old scarf to class. The design on it was simple: three lines and a small bird. "This came from my hometown," she said. "Nobody uses it now." We looked at it for a long time. Then Xiao Man asked a question. "Can we put it on our class T-shirt?" The teacher was so pleased that she agreed at once. We worked for two weeks. We made the bird a little bigger so that people could see it from far away. On sports day, forty students wore the same bird. Other classes asked where we got the design. It is such a small pattern that nobody looked at it for years. Now it runs across a playground every spring.

questions.q: What was on the old scarf?
options: Forty small birds.
A picture of the teacher's hometown.
Three lines and a small bird.
The name of the class.
questions.explanation: 'The design on it was simple: three lines and a small bird.'

questions.q: Why did the students make the bird bigger?
options: So that people could see it from far away.
Because the teacher asked them to.
Because the T-shirt was too large.
So that it could cover the three lines.
questions.explanation: 'We made the bird a little bigger so that people could see it from far away.'

questions.q: What happened to the old design in the end?
options: It was put back in the teacher's box.
It was sold to another class.
It was changed into three lines.
It came back to life on the students' T-shirts.
questions.explanation: 'On sports day, forty students wore the same bird.' 与 'Now it runs across a playground every spring.'

title: The tree at the corner
body: There is an old tree at the corner of our street. Nobody knows its age. Last year the road was made wider. Workers came with a machine, and the tree was in the way. That evening about thirty neighbours stood around it. Old Mr Lin brought a photo from many years ago. In the photo, a young man stood under the same tree with a bicycle. "That is my father," he said. The workers waited. The next week the plan changed, and the road turned a little so that the tree could stay. Now there is a small wooden sign beside it. Children read it on their way to school. The tree gives us shade in summer. It also gives us a place to stand together.

questions.q: Why was the tree in danger last year?
options: Because it was too old to stand.
Because the road was being made wider.
Because children climbed it every day.
Because Mr Lin wanted to move it.
questions.explanation: 'Last year the road was made wider. Workers came with a machine, and the tree was in the way.'

questions.q: What did Mr Lin bring that evening?
options: A wooden sign.
An old bicycle.
An old photo of his father.
A letter from the workers.
questions.explanation: 'Old Mr Lin brought a photo from many years ago. In the photo, a young man stood under the same tree with a bicycle. "That is my father," he said.'

options: The road was changed so that the tree could stay.
The tree was moved to another street.
The neighbours bought the land.
The workers cut down half of the tree.
questions.explanation: 'The next week the plan changed, and the road turned a little so that the tree could stay.'

title: Silk under glass
body: Every Saturday morning I work at our town museum. My job is easy: I stand near the silk room and answer questions. The room is dark. Visitors often ask why. "Light is not kind to silk," I tell them. "We keep the room dark so that the colours can last." Some people are surprised. They think a museum should be bright. Last month a boy of six asked the best question of the year. "Is the silk sleeping?" I said yes. He was so happy with the answer that he told every visitor at the door. Now I use his words too. The silk is sleeping, and we are keeping the room quiet for it. It is not a scientific answer. But it makes people walk more softly.

questions.q: Why is the silk room dark?
options: Because the lights are broken.
Because visitors like a quiet room.
So that the colours of the silk can last.
Because the museum saves money.
questions.explanation: 'We keep the room dark so that the colours can last.'

questions.q: What did the six-year-old boy ask?
options: Whether the silk was sleeping.
Why the room was so small.
How old the silk was.
Where the lights were.
questions.explanation: 'Last month a boy of six asked the best question of the year. "Is the silk sleeping?"'

questions.q: Why does the writer still use the boy's words?
options: Because the boy comes every Saturday.
Because the museum told him to.
Because it is a scientific answer.
Because it makes visitors move more quietly.
questions.explanation: 'It is not a scientific answer. But it makes people walk more softly.'
